facts: The respondent, Ashok Kumar Nigam, was appointed as District Government Counsel on September 17, 2004.
His term was renewed on March 3, 2006, for a period of one year and ended on March 5, 2007.
He submitted his application for renewal of his term on January 19, 2007.
The State Government refused his renewal on April 3, 2008, resulting in the cancellation of his engagement.
The respondent filed a writ petition before the High Court of Allahabad, Lucknow Bench, which was allowed on October 14, 2009.
The High Court set aside the order dated April 3, 2008, and granted further relief to the respondent.
issues: Whether the State Government has discretion to terminate the term of the District Government Counsel (Criminal)?
Whether the High Court exceeded its jurisdiction in setting aside the order dated April 3, 2008?
Whether the judgment of the High Court suffers from apparent errors?
petitioner_arguments: The respondent would only have a right of consideration and nothing more.
The High Court gave no reasons much less valid reasons for setting aside the order dated April 3, 2008.
respondent_arguments: The order dated April 3, 2008 was a non-speaking order and suffered from the vice of nonapplication of mind and was arbitrary.
The impugned order is contrary to the rules in force.
court_reasoning: The court held that the High Court did not exceed its jurisdiction in setting aside the order dated April 3, 2008.
The court also held that the judgment of the High Court does not suffer from apparent errors.
holding: Leave granted in all the Special Leave Petitions.
The appeals are dismissed as infructuous.
